title: Topological Fingerprints of Commensurate Order in Twisted Moiré Lattices
authors: Collin J. Kovacs, Jiangxu Li, Yang Zhang, Konstantinos D. Vogiatzis, Adrian Del Maestro, Vasileios Maroulas
abstract: Moiré patterns in twisted bilayer materials exhibit long-range periodic order that is highly sensitive to twist angle. Identifying commensurate angles from real-space atomic structures remains challenging, as spectral and geometric methods emphasize global periodicity and are sensitive to disorder and finite-size effects. Here, we introduce a data-driven topological framework that quantifies moiré periodicity by treating atomic configurations as point-cloud data and extracting multiscale signatures using persistent homology. At the core of our approach is a small-neighborhood separation filter that removes redundant local motifs in persistence diagrams while preserving key structural features, enabling sharp minima in Wasserstein distances between twisted and untwisted reference configurations that accurately recover commensurate angles. We benchmark this framework against geometric and spectral similarity measures and show that the resulting topological descriptors remain stable under positional disorder ranging from weak to strong perturbations in the bond length. We further transfer these descriptors using a constrained Gaussian process surrogate to sparsely sampled configurations of a twisted MoTe$_2$ dichalcogenide bilayer. These results establish topological descriptors with neighborhood separation as a robust framework for identifying commensurate order in moiré systems and tracking commensurate structural similarity under disorder, sparsity, and finite-size effects.
summary: This paper proposes a novel topological data analysis framework using persistent homology to robustly identify commensurate moiré order in twisted bilayer materials. By filtering out noise using a small-neighborhood separation technique, the authors show that their topological descriptors accurately pinpoint known commensurate angles even when the atomic structure is perturbed by disorder or sampled sparsely. This establishes a powerful, disorder-resilient tool for characterizing moiré superlattices.
main_problem: The primary challenge is developing a robust method to identify commensurate moiré order in twisted bilayer materials directly from atomic coordinates, overcoming limitations of traditional spectral or geometric methods sensitive to disorder.
main_result: The authors introduce a data-driven topological framework using persistent homology with a small-neighborhood separation filter, which successfully recovers sharp signatures corresponding to known commensurate angles even under significant positional disorder.
method: The method treats atomic configurations as point clouds and applies persistent homology to extract multiscale topological signatures. A key innovation is the small-neighborhood separation filter applied to persistence diagrams to enhance the signal related to periodicity.
model_or_system: The study focuses on Moiré patterns in twisted bilayer materials, using twisted MoTe2 dichalcogenide bilayers and twisted bilayer graphene as test cases. The analysis involves projecting 3D atomic coordinates into 2D point clouds.
key_observables: Topological descriptors derived from persistent homology, specifically sharp minima in Wasserstein distances between twisted and untwisted reference configurations, which correlate with commensurate angles.
important_parameters: Twist angle ($	heta$), disorder magnitude ($\epsilon$), and sampling ratio ($ho$) are key parameters used to test the robustness of the descriptor.
main_assumptions: The framework assumes that the topological signature of commensurate order manifests as a distinct, sharp feature (minimum) in the calculated topological distance metric.
figures_summary: Figures compare the performance of various structural descriptors (SSF, Hausdorff, PDs) for detecting commensurate order, showing that the proposed $\delta$-separated topological score yields the clearest and most robust correlation with known angles.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first identifying the limitations of existing methods, introducing the topological framework using persistent homology, benchmarking this framework against geometric/spectral measures, and finally demonstrating its robustness by testing it under controlled levels of positional disorder and sparsity.
why_interesting: While the focus is on structural characterization rather than quantum dynamics, the use of topological data analysis (TDA) to extract robust, symmetry-aware fingerprints from complex, disordered atomic structures is highly relevant for characterizing the underlying physical states in quantum materials.
